title: Pylon — Fwd Mount Side Link — Installation of the Aluminium Fitting with an Interference-Fit Bush
abstract: Replacement of the forward mount side link fitting by an aluminium item with an interference-fit bush at the lug bore and an increased lug edge distance, to slow the fretting found at entry into service.

sections.planning_reason: Fretting at the side link lug bore of the forward engine mount was found on aircraft flown at high thrust derates with frequent short sectors, and eight fittings were removed in the first eighteen months of operation, three of them at unscheduled events. The original bush retention relied on an adhesive bond that was not surviving the thermal cycle. This Service Bulletin introduces an interference-fit bush and a revised lug edge distance as the answer.
sections.description: The aluminium side link fitting is replaced by an item with an interference-fit bush at the lug bore and a 3 mm increase in lug edge distance. The pylon frame kit is retained and the rib is re-shimmed to hold the revised link geometry. The fitting is supplied as a completed assembly because the bush is cold expanded on a bench and not in situ.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove the engine to the procedure in the maintenance documentation and support the pylon on the fixture. Remove the pylon fairings to get access in zones 431 and 441. Do the removal steps of the mount removal task and take out the existing side link fitting. Clean the pylon faying surface and do a detailed visual inspection of it. Re-shim the rib D5450126830111 to the revised link geometry using the shim pack in the kit. Install the fitting supplied as a completed assembly; the bush is cold expanded on a bench and is never expanded in situ. Torque the joint in the sequence given in the accomplishment instructions and lockwire it. Refit the fairings with screws AES177340K7, install the engine and do an engine ground run. Enter the fitting serial number and the 24 000 flight cycle life limit in the life-limited parts record.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00212. Embodiment is one way: once the lug bore has been machined for the interference-fit bush the earlier fitting cannot be reinstalled.
sections.material_note: Kit K5450-1019-01 contains the two completed fitting assemblies, the shim packs and the fastener set for one aircraft. Lead time is twenty weeks. The removed fittings must be returned to Aeralis for the fleet fatigue survey.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next engine removal, and in any case within 60 months after the date of this Service Bulletin.

title: Pylon — Fwd Mount Side Link — Installation of the Aluminium Fitting with an Interference-Fit Bush

issue.reason: Closing effectivity statement issued in place of the open accomplishment, with a concession route that lets delivered kits and part-accomplished aircraft be finished to this standard.

abstract: Closed to new accomplishment. This Service Bulletin installed the aluminium side link fitting with an interference-fit bush; it is replaced by the steel fitting bulletin, with a concession route for delivered kits and for aircraft part way through the work.

sections.planning_reason: Fretting at the side link lug bore of the forward engine mount was found on aircraft flown at high thrust derates with frequent short sectors, and eight fittings were removed in the first eighteen months of operation. This Service Bulletin introduced an interference-fit bush and a revised lug edge distance as a first answer. In service it slowed the mechanism without removing it, and the 24 000 flight cycle life limit it carried proved unworkable for operators. The steel fitting standard replaces it. Withdrawing this Service Bulletin outright was not possible: twelve aircraft were part way through the work at the closing date and four operators had already taken delivery of kits that have no other use.
sections.description: The aluminium side link fitting is replaced by an item with an interference-fit bush at the lug bore and a 3 mm increase in lug edge distance. The pylon frame kit is retained and the rib is re-shimmed to hold the revised link geometry. The fitting is supplied as a completed assembly because the bush is cold expanded on a bench and not in situ.
sections.accomplishment_summary: This Service Bulletin is closed to new accomplishment. Do not start it on an aircraft that has not already been opened for it. Two routes remain. Route A, for an aircraft on which the lug bore has already been machined for the interference-fit bush: finish the work as written, enter the 24 000 flight cycle life limit and plan the steel standard at a later engine removal. Route B, for an operator holding delivered kits with no aircraft part way through: the kits may be consumed on any aircraft in the original effectivity under the concession reference given in the accomplishment instructions, provided the embodiment is notified to Aeralis before the work starts and the aircraft is entered on the steel standard retrofit plan at the same time. On every other aircraft, close the work package without action and plan the steel fitting bulletin instead.
sections.effectivity_note: Was applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00212. Closed to new accomplishment with effect from August 2019. The effectivity remains open for the twelve aircraft already opened for this work and for kits already delivered, both under the concession route in the accomplishment instructions. Aircraft already embodied keep their life-limited fitting and their tracked cycle count until the steel standard is applied; the configuration remains airworthy and no interim inspection is added by this revision.
sections.material_note: Kit K5450-1019-01 is withdrawn from the catalogue and no further kits will be built. Kits already delivered are not returnable, because the fittings are made to a completed-assembly standard that has no other application; they may instead be consumed under the concession route until the end of 2021, after which any remaining kit is scrapped against the operator letter that accompanied this revision.

type_data.compliance_time: Closed to new accomplishment. Aircraft already opened for this work, and delivered kits consumed under the concession route, before the end of 2021.

revision_history.reason: Closing effectivity statement and concession route for delivered kits
